To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we develop a new training method to simultaneously transfer both training and inference in deep neural networks to integers with high efficiency, which is promising for deployment in embedded systems and hardware accelerators.
we develop a new training method to discretize both weights and gradients in deep neural networks and achieve improved accuracy on multiple datasets.
we propose a new method termed WAGE to simultaneously reduce precision of weights, activations, gradients, and errors in deep neural networks.
In summary, our research is concerned with
an efficient and unified method to discretize deep neural networks with low bitwidths and low energy, which can be deployed for large scale and long time AI applications.
the discrete representation and deployment of neural networks, which is an emerging and important topic for the future AI applications.
an efficient and robust approach to training, quantizing, and transferring deep networks to embedded systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we develop the first training and inference method with pure discrete dataflow, and the method is simple, fast, and effective.
WAGE provides a new and practical way of discretization, which can be used to deploy both training and inference of neural networks in embedded systems with high performance and energy efficiency.

the proposed WAGE is the first to achieve training and inference simultaneously with discrete parameters, which is a significant step towards the deployment of deep neural networks in low-bitwidth and low-precision embedded devices.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
WAGE provides the first systematic way to train and deploy neural networks on low-bitwidth integers, and it is promising to be deployed for future hardware systems.
the quantization is not just a tool to reduce precision and speedup the inference, but also an effective way to improve accuracy.
the proposed WAGE can achieve a higher level of discretization for deep neural networks, and a higher level of quantization for deep neural network training.

it is possible to train and deploy a DNN with integer weights, activations and gradients.
discrete training and inference can be performed simultaneously, and the proposed method can be applied to a variety of hardware systems.
